text: When an iCE40 conv2d runs at 38.8 MHz with a timing violation from a fully combinational 9-multiplier product-adder tree whose core.out_data LUT4 stage has 12 cells and 10.57 ns of route, pipeline the multiplier outputs and split the adder tree with registers (tree_regs 0→3, pipe_mul 0→2) to cut the critical path from 25.77 ns to 15.35 ns and reach 65.1 MHz feasible for +70 LUTs.

When an iCE40 conv2d is already feasible at 65.1 MHz with a 24-bit accumulator and 286 LUTs, narrow the accumulator to the legal minimum 21 bits to cut 10 LUTs and raise Fmax to 67.5 MHz by shortening carry chains in the 9-term adder tree despite the critical path being row_cnt/row_ok_d control.

When the iCE40 conv2d is feasible at 67.5 MHz with the critical path entirely in control logic (core.row_cnt -> core.row_ok_d -> core.row_cnt, ~14.8 ns) and datapath slack, don't add multiplier input/output fabric registers or another multiplier stage—it leaves fmax at 67.5 MHz and costs 1 LUT; instead shorten the row_cnt/row_ok_d control path.

When iCE40 conv2d timing is limited by control logic row_cnt->row_ok_d (~14.8 ns) rather than the datapath, remove the DSP output register while retaining full multiplier-tree pipelining to gain +3.1 MHz (67.53->70.62 MHz) and save 4 LUTs (277->273) by freeing routing on the control path.

On ice40 conv2d, when the row-counter/row-valid control path (core.row_cnt/row_ok_d) is the critical path and the multiplier-to-tree datapath has slack, do not trim pipe_mul from 2 to 1 to save FFs: it added 2 LUTs and dropped Fmax by 1.5 MHz (70.6 to 69.1 MHz), since the control route (2.41 ns) still dominated the 14.48 ns path.

On iCE40 conv2d, when the datapath is fully pipelined and control logic is critical at 69.1 MHz with a 60 MHz target, do not cut tree_regs from 3 to 2 to save 6 LUTs; it makes the adder tree critical (15 LUT4s, 13.5 ns logic+route) and drops Fmax to 51.4 MHz, losing feasibility.

When an ice40 conv2d is timing-limited at 39 MHz by a routing-dominated 12-cell combinational product-adder LUT4 tree (7.43 ns logic + 11.76 ns route, 25.66 ns path), add 3 register levels to the adder tree and 2 pipeline stages after the multipliers, and narrow the accumulator from 24 to 21 bits, breaking the long LUT/route chain and shortening the carry chain to raise Fmax by 27.6 MHz to 66.6 MHz at +57 LUT and unchanged 0 DSP.

When an ice40 conv2d's unregistered multiplier outputs feed a 12-cell LUT4/route adder tree into the carry accumulator (25.66 ns, 39 MHz), insert 2 multiplier-output pipeline stages plus 3 adder-tree register levels and shrink the accumulator from 24 to 21 bits, raising Fmax to 66.6 MHz (+27.6 MHz) for +57 LUTs and 0 DSPs by breaking the long LUT/route chain into short registered stages.

For iCE40 conv2d, when Fmax is ~66.6 MHz and the critical path is routing through the combinational multiplier-output LUT/route tree into the carry-chain accumulator, adding one multiplier-output pipeline stage (pipe_mul 2→3) only yields +1.0 MHz and +3 LUTs (0 DSP) while shifting the critical path to core.row_cnt, so instead split the 9-term product-adder tree and shorten the accumulator carry chain.

When an ice40 conv2d multiply-add cone is timing-limited by a 25.66 ns routing-dominated unregistered LUT tree feeding a 24-bit carry-chain accumulator, insert 3 register levels in the product tree, 2 pipeline stages after the multipliers, and shrink the accumulator to 21 bits to break the path into short registered hops, raising Fmax from 39.0 to 66.6 MHz at +57 LUT and 0 DSP.

On iCE40 conv2d, when routing dominates the multiplier-to-accumulator path and par_rows is already at the throughput cap, push pipe_mul from 2 to 3 (one extra output register) rather than deeper restructuring: it yielded only 67.53 MHz from 66.57 MHz (+0.95 MHz) for +3 LUTs and remained infeasible, because the critical path shifted to core.row_cnt→core.row_ok_d control logic outside the multiply-add cone.

When iCE40 conv2d is timing-limited by routing on core.row_cnt→core.row_ok_d (14.81 ns total, 3.52 ns route) and resources are non-limiting, moving the post-multiplier register from fabric pipe_mul to dsp_regs=out at the same pipeline depth leaves Fmax at 67.53 MHz with 276 LUT/0 DSP, so fix the row-control route instead.

On an iCE40 conv2d timing-limited at 39.0 MHz by a routing-dominated 25.66 ns combinational 9-product multiplier→adder-tree→carry-chain accumulator path, insert 2 register stages after each multiplier, 3 registers inside the adder tree, and shrink acc_width from 24 to 21 to cut the path to 15.02 ns and raise Fmax to 66.6 MHz at +57 LUT and 0 DSP.

On iCE40 conv2d, don't move a multiplier-output pipeline stage from fabric pipe_mul to the DSP output register when the 15.02 ns critical path is the frame_start→row_cnt→row_ok_d routing path, since it gave 0 MHz (66.57 MHz unchanged, 273 LUT, 0 DSP) because that control-path route is unaffected by multiplier-boundary placement.

On iCE40 conv2d, when the critical path is routing-dominated in the row_cnt/row_ok_d control LUTs (DFF row_cnt → LUT row_cnt → LUT row_ok_d, 14.81 ns), don't add a multiplier-output pipeline stage (pipe_mul 1→3): it costs +3 LUTs for only +0.95 MHz (66.57→67.53 MHz) with no DSP change and leaves feasibility unchanged, so pipeline the control path instead.

When the ice40 conv2d critical path is control logic (core.frame_start→core.row_cnt→core.row_ok_d, ~15 ns) and the datapath has slack at a 60 MHz target, move the multiplier output register to the DSP boundary (pipe_mul 3→0, dsp_regs none→out) only for LUT minimization, since it saved 1 LUT but cost 1.4 MHz Fmax because the control path stayed critical.

When an ice40 conv2d is stuck at 66.11 MHz with the critical path in control (core.frame_start→core.row_cnt→core.row_ok_d, 15.13 ns, 9.02 ns LUT+route) and the multiplier tree has slack, dropping multiplier-output registers (pipe_mul→0-1, dsp_regs out→none) leaves Fmax, LUTs, and DSPs unchanged (66.11 MHz, 275 LUT, 0 DSP), so pipeline the row counter/comparator instead of paying for multiplier-output staging.

On iCE40 conv2d, when already feasible at 66.1 MHz with a routing-limited row_cnt/row_ok_d control path, adding a DSP output register and going pipe_mul 1→2 only reached 67.5 MHz (+1.4 MHz, +1 LUT) because the multiplier is already off the limiter—don't use multiplier staging to fix control-path timing.

When an iCE40 conv2d at 67.5 MHz is timing-limited by the 14.8 ns row_cnt→row_ok_d control route rather than the multiplier datapath, add the multiplier input register alongside the existing output register, which gives +1.5 MHz (69.1 MHz) for +1 LUT and 0 DSP by relieving shared routing congestion but stays neutral because the control path still dominates.

On iCE40 conv2d when Fmax is limited by routing through the frame_start->row_cnt->row_ok_d control chain (14.5 ns), adding both input and pipeline DSP-boundary registers (in_out + in_pipe_out) as route isolation made it worse, dropping Fmax from 69.1 to 64.7 MHz (-4.4 MHz) with 0 LUT/DSP change, because it did not touch that control path—row_cnt route delay rose from 2.41 to 2.85 ns—so reserve DSP-boundary re-timing for multiplier-limited paths, not control-routing limiters.

When an iCE40 conv2d is timing-limited by a 24-bit unregistered 12-LUT4 product/adder tree and long routing (25.66 ns before), pipeline the 9-term tree with 3 register levels, add 2 multiplier-output stages, and narrow acc_width 24->21 (the legal 8+8+4+1 minimum), which shortens the carry chain and lifts Fmax 39.0->66.6 MHz for +57 LUT and no DSP.

On iCE40 conv2d with an already feasible 66.57 MHz design whose critical path is routing-dominated in core.row_cnt/core.row_ok_d (15.02 ns total, 2.95 ns route), leave pipe_mul unchanged instead of setting it to [2,1]: the move costs 2 LUT and 0.46 MHz (66.57→66.11 MHz) while doing nothing for timing because the multiplier is not on that critical path.

On ice40 conv2d, when Fmax is stuck at 66.1 MHz by routing-dominated control paths such as row_cnt→row_ok_d despite only 275 LUT/0 DSP used, adding a multiplier output register and increasing pipe_mul from 1 to 2 gains only +1.4 MHz (to 67.5 MHz) at +1 LUT and 0 DSP and remains infeasible, so retime or duplicate the row_cnt/row_ok_d control logic instead of further pipelining the multiplier.

On iCE40 conv2d, when a fully combinational multiplier-to-accumulator cone with a 24-bit carry chain limits Fmax to 39.0 MHz, insert 2 fabric pipeline stages after each multiplier plus 3 adder-tree levels and narrow acc_width to 21 to reach 66.6 MHz (+27.6 MHz) for +57 LUT and 0 DSP by breaking the 25.66 ns LUT/route path into short registered hops.

When ice40 conv2d is timing-infeasible at ~66.6 MHz with a 15.0 ns routing-dominated critical path through core.row_cnt→core.row_ok_d, adding multiplier-output fabric registers (none→out) only reaches 67.5 MHz (+1.0 MHz) at +3 LUTs and stays infeasible because the real limiter is the row_cnt→row_ok_d control net, not the multiplier→tree hop—so retime or break the actual control net instead.

When an ice40 conv2d is already feasible at 67.5 MHz with the critical path entirely in control routing (row_cnt→row_ok_d, 14.8 ns, ~3.5 ns route) and throughput maxed at 1 pixel/cycle, don't strip one fabric register after each of the 9 multipliers to free placement, because it only cuts LUTs 276→275 and drops Fmax to 66.1 MHz by shifting criticality to frame_start→row_cnt→row_ok_d (15.1 ns); instead attack the control net's routing/congestion since the multiplier/tree datapath has slack.

When an iCE40 conv2d is feasible but Fmax is routing-limited by a control path (frame_start→row_cnt→row_ok_d, 15.13 ns) while the datapath has slack, add a multiplier input register alongside its output register (pipe_mul 1→2, dsp_regs none→in_out) to relieve shared routing congestion on the tiny control net, raising Fmax 66.1→69.1 MHz at +2 LUT and no DSP.

When an iCE40 conv2d is timing-closed at 39.0 MHz by a 25.66 ns routing-dominated 12-LUT combinational product/adder cone that collapses 9 multiplier products into a 24-bit carry chain and throughput is already maxed at par_rows=3, split the cone with 3 registered adder-tree hops plus 2 post-multiplier pipeline stages and narrow the accumulator to 21 bits, reaching 66.6 MHz (+27.6 MHz) at +57 LUT and 0 DSP.

When iCE40 conv2d is routing-limited at 66.6 MHz by a combinational 9-product multiplier/adder tree feeding the 24-bit carry-chain accumulator, skip the third multiplier pipeline stage (pipe_mul 2->3) because it only moves the critical path to core.row_cnt/core.row_ok_d and buys +0.95 MHz (to 67.5 MHz) for +3 LUTs with no DSP change, and instead register or narrow the accumulator path.

When an iCE40 conv2d is already feasible at 67.5 MHz with the minimum 21-bit accumulator and its critical path is the routing-dominated row_cnt/row_ok_d control net, do not widen acc_width to 42: it adds 82 LUTs and makes a 39-LUT out_data arithmetic chain the 18.47 ns critical path, dropping Fmax to 54.1 MHz; leave acc_width at 21 and relieve the control routing instead.

On iCE40 conv2d, when timing fails through the multiplier-to-accumulator LUT path with a 42-bit accumulator, narrow the accumulator to the legal 21 bits and register both multiplier input and output; LUTs fall 358→277 and Fmax rises 54.1→64.7 MHz by isolating the product bus from the adder tree and relieving routing on the shared control net.

On an iCE40 conv2d, when a feasible design is timing-limited by a routing-heavy control path (frame_start→row_cnt→row_ok_d, 15.46 ns) rather than the multiplier tree, set the multiplier-boundary registers to input+output to relieve shared routing; Fmax rises from 64.69 to 69.07 MHz (+4.38 MHz) with LUT 277 and DSP 0 unchanged.

When an iCE40 conv2d at 69.1 MHz is feasible but timing-limited by the routing-dominated control cone frame_start→row_cnt→row_ok_d→row_cnt (14.48 ns), do not add full multiplier input+pipe+output registers (dsp_regs=out,in_pipe_out) to relieve it: it drops FMAX to 63.8 MHz (−5.3 MHz) at unchanged 277 LUTs/0 DSPs because the extra FF banks increase congestion rather than shortening the control nets.

When an ice40 conv2d is feasible but routing-limited on the control cone row_cnt→row_ok_d (~15.7 ns), cut pipe_mul from 3 to 2 stages after each of the 9 multipliers to remove nine product-width FF banks, freeing routing channels and compacting placement so Fmax rises 63.82→67.53 MHz (+3.7 MHz) even at a small datapath cost.

When the iCE40 conv2d is feasible at 67.5 MHz with control routing (row_cnt→row_ok_d) critical, do not drop the adder-tree pipeline level (tree_regs 3→2) to relieve that congestion—doing so exposes a 15-LUT t3 datapath with 7.0 ns route and drops Fmax to 51.6 MHz, losing feasibility.

When an ice40 conv2d is timing-limited by a 25.66 ns routing-dominated unregistered 24-bit product-adder cone into the output accumulator, insert 2 multiplier pipeline stages and 3 adder-tree registers and narrow acc_width to 21 bits, which shortens the carry chain and breaks the cone into registered hops, raising Fmax from 38.97 to 66.57 MHz for +57 LUT and 0 DSP.

When ice40 conv2d is routing-limited at 66.57 MHz with no DSPs and a 15.0 ns DFF→LUT4→LUT4 path through row_cnt/row_ok_d, changing pipe_mul to [2,1] adds 2 LUTs and lowers Fmax to 66.11 MHz without shortening the critical path, so leave the multiplier pipeline as-is and instead add registers/narrow the accumulator tree.

When ice40 conv2d is already feasible at 66.1 MHz with maxed 1 pixel/cycle throughput and the critical path is control (core.frame_start→core.row_cnt→core.row_ok_d at 15.13 ns), do not replace two fabric multiplier-output pipeline stages with a single DSP-output register (pipe_mul [1,0], dsp_regs none→out): it saves 0 LUT, 0 DSP, and 0 MHz because the datapath is not critical.

When an ice40 conv2d is already feasible at 66.1 MHz with the critical path in control routing (frame_start→row_cnt→row_ok_d at 15.02 ns), enabling one multiplier output pipeline stage (pipe_mul 0→1) cut 2 LUTs (275→273) and raised Fmax only 0.5 MHz to 66.6 MHz, so use it for LUT reduction only, not for timing, because the control path remains critical.

When an iCE40 conv2d is feasible at 66.6 MHz with 273 LUT and its 15.02 ns critical path is the control cone frame_start->row_cnt->row_ok_d rather than the multiplier/adder tree, do not cut tree_regs from 3 to 2 (even with a DSP-output register) to save LUT: the tree route/carry path becomes 19.44 ns, dropping Fmax by 15.1 MHz to 51.4 MHz and losing feasibility for only -4 LUT.

When iCE40 conv2d timing fails with tree_regs=2 and a 15-cell LUT4/route cone from t1 to t3 (6.38 ns logic + 7.13 ns route), restore tree_regs=3 to break that cone and move the critical path to control logic, raising Fmax from 51.4 to 67.5 MHz for +7 LUT and 0 DSP.

When an iCE40 conv2d is feasible but timing-limited at 67.5 MHz by a 14.81 ns routing-dominated control cone (row_cnt→row_ok_d), do not repack the multiplier registers for resource savings—switching to input+output multiplier registers with a single fabric pipe stage ([3,1]/in_out) gives 0 MHz, 0 LUT, and 0 DSP change because the critical path never enters the multiplier.

When an iCE40 conv2d is feasible at 67.5 MHz with LUT=276 and the 14.81 ns critical arc is the row_cnt->row_ok_d control routing cone while the datapath has slack, adding a multiplier output boundary register to the pipe_mul=2 design leaves Fmax/LUT/DSP unchanged, so optimize the control cone rather than the multiplier pipeline.

When an ice40 conv2d is routing-limited at 67.5 MHz by the core.row_cnt→row_ok_d control arc (~14.8 ns) while the datapath has slack, registering the multiplier input+output (dsp_regs=out,in_out) shortens that arc to 14.5 ns and moves the critical start to core.frame_start, but yields only +1.5 MHz at +1 LUT (69.1 MHz, 277 LUT), so skip it when LUT reduction is the remaining objective.
